chapters.1: Peter encourages believers to grow in a chain of qualities, including faith, goodness, knowledge, self-control, and love, so their faith becomes fruitful rather than stagnant. Sensing his death is near, he insists that the message about Christ's power and return isn't based on invented stories but on his own eyewitness experience of Christ's glory and on the trustworthy, Spirit-inspired word of the prophets.
chapters.2: Peter warns strongly against false teachers who will arise among believers, bringing destructive teachings and exploiting people through greed. He points to past examples of God's judgment, including rebellious angels, the flood, and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, to show that God knows how to judge the ungodly while rescuing the godly, and describes these false teachers as morally corrupt and spiritually empty, leading people back into the sin they had escaped.
chapters.3: Peter addresses scoffers who mock the idea of Christ's return, arguing that God's sense of timing isn't the same as ours and that his patience, not inactivity, delays judgment so more people can repent. He describes a future day when the heavens and earth as we know them will be dissolved and replaced with a new heaven and new earth where righteousness dwells, and urges believers to live holy lives while they wait, growing in grace and the knowledge of Christ.
